title: ee says /ee/
parentNote: Two e's side by side say ee, as in bee, tree and sheep. After a fortnight of silent e this one is a relief: the letters are right next to each other, they always say the same thing, and there is no rule to remember. The slip to watch for is the short e coming back, so feed is read as fed and sleep as slip — that one letter of difference is the whole lesson, so say the pair yourself and let them hear it: fed, feed. ship, sheep. Point at the two e's as one chunk, not as e and then e, the same way you did with ie and ue. Pull your lips wide into a smile and hold it — eee — and if they are enjoying it, hunt for ee on the cereal box at breakfast; it is one of the easiest spellings to spot in the wild.

activities.mouthCue: Pull your lips wide into a smile, teeth almost shut, and hold it: eee.
activities.prompt: Two of the same letter, standing together. They do not say e and then e. Together they say ee.
One of these is a team of two letters. The other two work on their own.
Three teams, three different sounds. Find the one that says ee.
Only two sounds in this word. The ee is one of them.
Now the team is in the middle. Keep it in one piece and add the d.
Four sounds: s, then l, then the team, then p.
The longest one. Three sounds crowd in at the front before the team.
One floats and one says baa. Listen hard to the middle.
One e, or two? Listen to the middle sound.
Same ending. Only the sound at the very front is different.

activities.text: A bee sat on the green tree and did not see Meg.
Did Sam feed the three sheep at the gate?
Sweet grass is the best bit, and the sheep sleep in it.

activities.title: Three sheep on the street
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Three sheep got free and ran up the street.
Meg did see them at the green gate.
Sam ran up with sweet feed in a red tin.
The sheep did stop and did sniff at the tin.
Sam did shake the tin, and the sheep did keep up with him!
Meg did shut the gate, and the three sheep did get in.
Then Meg did see the dog with the red tin.
The dog ate the sweet feed. The dog did sleep till three!
